# Gladly MCP Server
for AI Agents
Connect your AI agent to StackOne's Gladly MCP server and give it 65 MCP tools out of the box. Auth, tool execution, and security all managed.

### 65 Agent Actions
Create, read, update, and delete across Gladly — and extend your agent's capabilities with custom actions.
![](/_astro/light-orange-fingerprint.R770-NAv.svg)
Authentication
### Agent Tool Authentication
Per-user OAuth in one call. Your Gladly MCP server gets session-scoped tokens with zero credentials stored on your infra.

### Agent Protection
Every Gladly tool response scanned for prompt injection in milliseconds — 88.7% accuracy, all running on CPU.

A Gladly MCP server lets AI agents read and write Gladly data through the [Model Context Protocol](/platform/mcp/) — Anthropic's open standard for connecting LLMs to external tools. StackOne's Gladly MCP server ships with 65 pre-built actions, fully extensible via the [Connector Builder](/platform/ai-integration-builder/) — plus managed authentication, prompt injection defense, observability, and agent execution runtime. Connect it from MCP clients like [Claude Desktop](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/claude-desktop/), [Claude Code](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/claude-code/), [Cursor](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/cursor/), [Goose](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/goose/), and VS Code, or from agent frameworks like OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, and Vercel AI SDK.

Does StackOne have a Gladly MCP server?
Yes. StackOne offers a hosted Gladly MCP server with 65 pre-built actions, and every action is tested and QA'd by StackOne. Connect it to [Claude](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/claude-desktop/), [Cursor](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/cursor/), and any other [MCP client](/platform/mcp/), or to any agent framework through the [AI Action SDK](https://docs.stackone.com/agents/typescript/introduction). title: Gladly MCP server for Claude & ChatGPT | usefulapi
snippet:
# Gladly MCP server
Find customers, read conversations, items and tasks; add internal notes in Gladly. Hosted by **usefulapi**: connect it to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client.

### Pull up a customer and review their conversations
Find a customer by email, phone number or external id. Then list their conversations with topics, status and assignee, oldest first, so an agent sees the history.
### Read the timeline of one conversation
Open a conversation and list its messages, emails, calls and notes in order. Ask the assistant for a short summary before you take over the case.
### Check which tasks are still open for a customer
List the open tasks of a customer with assignee and due date. Use it to see which follow-ups are late before you answer the customer.
### Map topics, inboxes and agents to names
Turn the topic, inbox and agent ids of a conversation into names. Use it to see who owns the case and where it sits.
### Add an internal note after a customer contact
Write an internal note on a conversation, for example a call back request. Only agents see the note. Each call adds a new note.
Changes data
## How do I connect Gladly?
### Before you connect
The login page asks for your **Gladly organization**, **Agent email** and **Gladly API token**.
Create the token in Gladly → **Settings → API → Create API token**. The agent needs the API User permission. The token is used only to call the Gladly API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.
### Claude claude.ai · Desktop
1. Open **Customize → Connectors**, then click **+ Add → Add custom connector**.
2. Enter the name **Gladly** and this URL, then click **Add**:
https://gladly.usefulapi.io/mcp
3. Claude opens the login page: enter your **Gladly organization**, **Agent email** and **Gladly API token**.
4. In a chat, click **+ → Connectors** and turn on **Gladly**.
Team and Enterprise: an Owner adds the connector for the organization first.
### ChatGPT chatgpt.com
1. Open [Plugins](https://chatgpt.com/plugins), click **+**, then **Add custom MCP server**.
2. Enter the name **Gladly** and this URL, choose **OAuth** as the authentication, confirm the warning and create it:
https://gladly.usefulapi.io/mcp
3. ChatGPT opens the login page: enter your **Gladly organization**, **Agent email** and **Gladly API token**.
4. In Plugins, install **Gladly**, then choose it in a chat.

title: Connect Gladly to ChatGPT: Manage Customers, Tasks, and Support Data
snippet:
If you are building support agents or automating helpdesk triage, you need to connect Gladly to ChatGPT. This requires a [Model Context Protocol (MCP) server](/what-is-mcp-and-mcp-servers-and-how-do-they-work/) - a dedicated translation layer that sits between ChatGPT's tool calls and Gladly's REST APIs. You can either build and maintain this infrastructure yourself, or use a managed integration platform like Truto to dynamically generate a secure, authenticated MCP server URL.

Giving a Large Language Model (LLM) read and write access to a live customer service environment is a serious engineering challenge. Gladly is architected entirely differently from standard ticketing systems like Zendesk or Jira. If you decide to [build a custom MCP server](/the-hands-on-guide-to-building-mcp-servers-for-ai-agents-2026/), you are responsible for managing OAuth lifecycles, mapping massive JSON schemas to MCP tool definitions, and dealing with Gladly's unique person-centric data models. Every time Gladly updates an endpoint, you have to update your server code, redeploy, and test the integration.
This guide breaks down exactly how to use Truto to generate a secure, managed MCP server for Gladly, connect it natively to ChatGPT, and execute complex support workflows using natural language.
## The Engineering Reality of the Gladly API
A custom MCP server is a [self-hosted integration layer](/how-to-architect-a-multi-tenant-mcp-server-for-enterprise-b2b-saas/). While Anthropic's open standard provides a predictable way for models to discover tools, implementing it against vendor APIs requires navigating undocumented behaviors and strict rate limits. You aren't just writing HTTP requests; you are translating an LLM's unpredictable output into strict API contracts.

Instead of writing and hosting custom connector code, Truto allows you to expose any connected Gladly account as a fully functional MCP server instantly.
Truto automatically derives the MCP tools from its internal documentation and schema definitions. It reads the exact capabilities of the Gladly API and generates the corresponding JSON schemas required by the MCP specification. Every server is backed by a secure cryptographic token scoped to a single authenticated Gladly instance.

To connect Gladly to ChatGPT, you first need to provision the MCP server. Truto gives you two ways to do this: manually via the UI, or programmatically via the API.
